title: Small elements escaping a sequence of finite p-adic subfields
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, the normed field $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with an absolute value extending $|\cdot|_\ell$ and its induced topology. Let $(F_k)_{k\geq0}$ be any sequence of intermediate fields $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq F_k\subseteq\Omega$, each finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. There exist elements $a_k\in\Omega\setminus F_k$ with $|a_k|\leq\ell^{-k}$ for all $k\geq0$. In particular $a_k\to0$ in $\Omega$. No nesting or exhaustion assumption on the fields $F_k$, and no completeness of $\Omega$, is required.

proof.text: For each $k$, restrict the given absolute value of $\Omega$ to $F_k$. It extends $|\cdot|_\ell$, and $F_k/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite-dimensional by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] to this restriction. Clause 4 supplies a nonzero uniformizer $\pi_k$ in $\mathfrak m_{F_k}$, so $\rho_k=|\pi_k|$ satisfies $0<\rho_k<1$. Clauses 1 and 5 give, for every $x\in F_k^\times$, a factorization $x=u\pi_k^m$ with $|u|=1$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. All these norms are restrictions of the original norm on $\Omega$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written arithmetic auxiliary for the noncomplete algebraic-closure coefficient obstruction; uniformizer and scaling argument made explicit.

proof.text: By algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the nonconstant polynomial $X^2-\pi_k$ has a root $b_k\in\Omega$. Thus $b_k^2=\pi_k$ and $|b_k|^2=\rho_k$, so $0<|b_k|<1$. If $b_k\in F_k$, its factorization from [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] would give $|b_k|=\rho_k^m$. For $m\leq0$ this is at least $1$, a contradiction. For $m\geq1$ it gives $\rho_k=\rho_k^{2m}\leq\rho_k^2<\rho_k$, again a contradiction. These cases exhaust the integers. Hence $b_k\notin F_k$. Choose these roots for all $k$ by classical choice.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written arithmetic auxiliary for the noncomplete algebraic-closure coefficient obstruction; uniformizer and scaling argument made explicit.

proof.text: Set $a_k=\ell^k b_k$. The factor $\ell^k$ is nonzero in $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq F_k$, so $a_k\in F_k$ would give $b_k=\ell^{-k}a_k\in F_k$, impossible. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $|a_k|=\ell^{-k}|b_k|<\ell^{-k}$, giving the weak bound also at $k=0$. For convergence, $\ell^0=1$ and, if $\ell^k\geq k+1$, then $\ell^{k+1}\geq2(k+1)\geq k+2$, since $\ell\geq2$. Thus $\ell^k\geq k+1$ by induction. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose an integer $N\geq0$ with $N+1>1/\varepsilon$. For $k\geq N$, $|a_k|\leq\ell^{-k}\leq(k+1)^{-1}\leq(N+1)^{-1}<\varepsilon$. This is convergence to $0$ for the given absolute value. Each $F_k$ was treated separately; no nesting, exhaustion or completeness was used.
